lines.text: Do you know how end-to-end encryption works? It's the little padlock in your chat app. And it means even the company can't read your messages.
Normally, a message travels through a company's server. Whoever runs that server could read it, or hand it over.
With end-to-end encryption, every phone makes two keys. A public key it shares with anyone, and a private key that never leaves the phone.
Think of the public key as an open padlock. Anyone can snap it shut. But only the matching private key can open it again.
So your friend's phone locks the message with your padlock before it leaves. The server only ever sees scrambled noise.
It arrives on your phone, and your private key opens it. Nobody in between ever held that key.
Could someone just guess the key? A two hundred fifty six bit key has a seventy eight digit number of possibilities. Every computer on Earth would need far longer than the age of the universe.
The catch: it protects messages on the way. It can't help if someone gets into your unlocked phone.
Orbi Transfer locks files right on your device too, with AES two fifty six. Add a passcode, and the key is made from it on your phone. It's never sent.
